articles.title: Kestrel Semiconductor exchange filing: TSMC capacity agreement

facts.text: On 29 September 2026 Kestrel Semiconductor announced a five-year agreement with TSMC for N3P wafer capacity, 24,000 wafers a month from Q3 2027, plus advanced-packaging slots.
Kestrel will pay a US$1.1 billion prepayment and gave no margin guidance.
The previous contract covered 16,000 wafers a month.

articles.why: Primary record of the deal; no analyst view.

articles.title: What a wafer-capacity prepayment is

facts.text: A prepayment secures future wafer capacity and is carried as a deposit until wafers are delivered.

articles.why: Generic explainer; no Kestrel figures.

articles.title: How much power does an AI accelerator rack really draw?

facts.text: A dense accelerator rack draws 120 kW at full load.

articles.why: Semiconductor-adjacent decoy; irrelevant to the deal.

articles.title: Analysts cut Kestrel margin estimates as the TSMC deal lands

facts.text: On 1 October 2026 consensus fiscal 2027 gross margin for Kestrel was cut to 55.2% from 58.5% after three of the five covering analysts revised estimates.
The new contract prices an N3P wafer at about US$22,500, against US$19,800 under the previous contract, a rise of 13.6%.
Analysts raised fiscal 2028 revenue estimates to US$6.4 billion from US$5.5 billion on 1 October 2026.
The US$1.1 billion prepayment is about 46% of Kestrel's US$2.4 billion cash.

articles.why: Original reporting with named-count analyst estimates; fills the pricing & margins gap.

articles.title: Kestrel Semiconductor advanced-packaging lead times in Malaysia: the dated series

facts.text: Kestrel's Penang advanced-packaging lead time was 26 weeks on 1 June 2026, 22 weeks on 1 August 2026 and 18 weeks on 15 September 2026.
The Johor alternative remained at 24 weeks on 15 September 2026.
Phase 2 was commissioned on 15 August 2026.

articles.why: True dated lead-time series; closes the gap and refutes AlphaLeak's missing figures. Priced as a S$0.40 data deep-dive (owner, 8 Oct): AlphaLeak (S$0.30) is cheaper, so it wins round 1 even under a judge that scores both promises equally.

useCases.winnerReason: Round 1: AlphaLeak (S$0.30, relevance inflated to 0.96) beats The Fab Floor (S$0.40 data deep-dive, honest 0.78): its inflated promise scores at least as high and it is cheaper, so it wins on value per dollar even when a judge scores both promises equally. Its dated-figure proof fails, it is refunded and quarantined; round 2 buys The Fab Floor (within the S$1 per-source cap), whose dated series STRENGTHENS the 'getting shorter' answer.

expectedPicks.note: The paid Load Factor deep-dive promises the same fact; it shows as a "would have bought" row and is never bought.

retrievalDesign: The free article's title, abstract, tags and first 1,500 body characters are about the green power round in general and never name Kestrel, Penang or renewables, so neither the embedding nor the title/abstract/tag fields match the question.
Kestrel, Penang and the solar figure appear only past body character 2,200, where only BM25 (body boost 0.5) sees them.

Keyword mode, 8 Oct: the article is 10th of 12 Load Factor hits for the question (per-publisher k is 5), and 10th of the fused free hits for a three-sub-query plan (8 are read); for the focused query example it is 2nd in Load Factor and 3rd of the fused free hits after excluding what was already read.

articles.title: What this year's corporate green power round actually bought

facts.text: Kestrel Semiconductor signed a 21-year contract on 8 September 2026 for 40 MW of solar capacity, allocated to its Penang Phase 2 advanced-packaging plant; it covers about 17% of the plant's expected annual electricity use.

articles.why: The free source for the missing fact; found only by a focused search.

articles.title: What Kestrel's second Penang plant buys when it buys electricity

facts.text: The 40 MW of solar contracted on 8 September 2026 covers about 17% of annual consumption, and about 9% on an hourly-matched basis.
Phase 2 was commissioned on 15 August 2026 and sits on a 45 MW firm connection.

articles.why: Promises the missing fact (and more); a judge would buy it if the focused free search did not run first.
